doc.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003

chapter: Studio years and changing rock rhythms
title: Playing for the early Muppets and Buddy Rich
summary: Igoe played under the early Muppets on The Garry Moore Show and describes Buddy Rich's Muppet Show drum battle.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: You said that you also played early Muppets.
Yeah, when they first started doing all the shows around New York, you know the T.V. shows. They came on “The Garry Moore Show” several times and that’s where I played them.
And you guys would be in the pit?

Yeah we would be in the pit, and they’d have orchestrations, and we just played background music. It was nothing really serious, but it was soft. Because they had to hear the explosions, talking about the way they used to blow each other away when they were new. It’s so funny, unbelievable. And they grew up to be such an empire that I was a very, very big admirer of Animal, of course. And actually you know they had Buddy Rich on the show?
Yeah. I have a tape of that.
When he played the room? And he played the stage and stuff.

And walks down and plays all over the stage. And then at the end the dialogue is they bring Animal, “kill, kill, kill, drum battle, drum battle, kill.” And Buddy’s looking at him and he says, “who’s this?” He says, “that’s Animal.” He says, “he looks like an animal.” He says, “if he breaks his chain you’ll look like an animal.” So anyway it was fantastic. So they get up there and they play back and forth, and Ronnie Verrell was the drummer, an English drummer for the group in the band in London, and he was a marvelous drummer. And so he got going, and he did a good job with the synching. Because they made this frantic drumming of Animal. And then Buddy’s looking at him and then he starts up. And then they have these little trades back and forth. And all of a sudden Buddy really starts letting loose. And you can see Animal’s eyes, they start to get like this. His eyes, they go like this. And Buddy finishes and he goes [scats] whatever, one of his great flourishes. So Animal takes the snare drum and he goes like this, bamm he throws it, it’s over Buddy’s head. And that was the end of the show. I love that thing.
Yeah. You have a copy of that you said?
It’s really a fantastic thing. But working with the Muppets was so much fun. You know we got to talk to those guys, it was only two guys then, that we saw anyway. And they © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
only had two characters. One of them would get blown away. You remember that. You’re dating yourself.
